description.short: One of India's oldest tea terroirs, noted for its pale liquor and delicate almond fragrance
description.overview: Kangra Valley is among the earliest tea regions planted by the British in the western Himalayas, possessing a distinct microclimate and its own Geographical Indication separate from Darjeeling.
description.aroma: Delicate, light almond and floral bouquet
description.taste: Smooth, gentle, subtle nutty undertones without heavy tannins
description.processing: Plucking → withering → rolling → moderate oxidation → drying

history.origin: Tea gardens in Kangra Valley were initiated by the British in the 1850s, making it one of India's earliest commercial tea areas alongside Darjeeling.
history.development: A catastrophic earthquake in 1905 leveled factories and infrastructure across the valley, severely setting back its industry compared to competitors in Darjeeling and Assam.
history.modern: Today, Kangra holds a protected Geographical Indication (GI) and is regaining prominence as a boutique region prized for subtle, green-leaning black teas.
interestingFacts: Despite its deep historic roots, Kangra remains far lesser-known abroad than Darjeeling, despite sharing similar Himalayan ancestry and varietal stock.
The devastating 1905 Kangra earthquake is widely cited as the principal event that derailed the valley from rivaling Darjeeling's global standing.
